answer: Each agent may propose a trade, but settlement requires a bonded account that has completed a jetty of unrelated transactions with independently bonded counterparties. A grove of fresh identities cannot manufacture that history by trading among itself, because those links share the same funding source and do not count. The attacker must lock separate capital behind each identity and pay real counterparties and fees over time; velvet-smooth scripts cannot recover those costs if the accounts are later exposed and slashed.
